summary: Elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects during tenant concurrency ramp caused by autoscaler oscillation and TLS session churn
description: Issue summary: During a customer-triggered concurrency increase (tenant scale-up) for Cortexa Labs' dedicated pool, they observed a sustained rise in 5xx responses from the public API and frequent streaming session disconnects. Impact: multiple generation requests returned 502/503 and long-lived streaming sessions dropped mid-response, causing user-visible failures in Cortexa's chat UI and automated ingestion pipelines. Scope: impacts single dedicated tenant pool in us-east-1 with pinned redwood-v1-large model. No configuration changes from customer other than increasing concurrency target in their dashboard.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer increases concurrency target from 50 -> 250 via Dedicated console for tenant-xxxx. 2) Start steady ramp of streaming sessions and short chat generation requests across 10s of clients. 3) Observe increased HTTP 5xx at API gateway and dropped streaming half-closed connections. 4) Revert concurrency target -> partial recovery observed.
observed_behavior:
- API gateway 502/503 rate climbs from baseline ~0.2% to 8-12% during ramp.
- Streaming connections see half-close/h2 stream errors and client resets.
- Serving runtime shows worker preemption and repeated model load/unload cycles.
- TLS session cache invalidation spikes, resulting in handshake backlog at proxy layer.

metrics_snapshot: 5xx_rate: baseline 0.2% -> peak 11.6% over 10m; p95 latency generation: 420ms -> 1.8s; runtime_gpu_util: 72% -> 91% with oscillation; autoscaler_events: 23 removes / 18 adds in 12m; tls_session_evictions/sec: 0.5 -> 67
investigation_notes: Support triage: confirmed customer saw errors at the same time as scale-up. SRE findings: 1) Autoscaler behaved aggressively under sudden connection ramp, removing/adding ephemeral workers to rebalance load which caused TLS session invalidation and KV cache thrash. 2) TLS session eviction led to handshake queueing at proxy which amplified apigw retries and caused downstream RSTs on long-lived http2 streams. 3) Serving runtime entered a model reload loop for a subset of ephemeral workers because KV cache misses triggered a fallback kernel path causing increased memory pressure and occasional watchdog restarts. Hypothesis: combination of (a) concurrency ramp, (b) autoscaler consolidation policy, and (c) TLS session eviction limits produced a feedback loop that amplified 5xx. Correlated dashboards: tenant-xxxx apigw logs, autoscaler audit, runtime evictions dashboards.
temporary_workaround:
- Advised customer to revert concurrency target to previous level (50) which reduced 5xx.
- Manually whitelisted tenant in autoscaler to avoid aggressive consolidation during warmup.
- Enabled short-lived keepalive extension on proxy to preserve sessions during ephemeral node replacement.
next_steps:
1) SRE to tune autoscaler consolidation cooldown for dedicated pools (follow-up RFC).
2) Engineering to add soft-stall for TLS session cache eviction during tenant warmup.
3) Runtime team to investigate KV cache pre-warming for scaled-up tenants to avoid model reload loops.
4) Capture an automated test scenario to reproduce ramp in staging.
5) Postmortem and customer RCA delivery.
resolution: in-progress: partial mitigation applied (whitelist + revert) restored service for customer. Full fixes pending cross-team changes listed in next_steps.
